Md. Mamtaz Uddin Ahmed, J:- In all these writ petitions the petitioners are different but the respondents are common and the writ petition arose out of cancellation of long term lease of Hotel Motel Zone of Cox's Bazar by the Ministry of Land through Deputy Commissioner Cox's Bazar by order dated 12.1.2010 but containing the similar facts and circumstances and involving similar issues.

2. In view of such position, all these Rules are heard together and disposed of by a single judgment.

3. The Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memo No.জঃপ্র/কক্ছ/রাজস্ব/২৪-৫৯/২০০৯-১০৫ dated 12.01.2010 (Annexure-A) issued by respondent No. I Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar cancelling the allotment of land measuring about 1.00 acre contained in B.S. Khatian No.01 corresponding to B.S. Plot No. 20002. 20003, Road No. 2 Plot No. 16 situated in Mouza- Jhilangja , P.S. Cox's Bazar at the Hotel/Motel Zone of Cox's Bazar and directing the petitioner to hand over possession should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

4. Pending hearing of the Rule, let the operation of the Memo No জঃপ্র/কক্ছ/রাজস্ব/২৪-৫৯/২০০৯-১০৫ dated 12.01.2010 issued by respondent No. 3, Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar be stayed for a period of 2(two) months from date.

5. In W.P. No. 639 of 2009 it has been stated that in the year 2002 the respondent No.3 invited applications for allotment of plots in the Hotel/Motel Zone of Cox's Bazar for the purpose of constructing 1-5 star hotels and motels in the said area. Accordingly, petitioner No.1 applied for allotment of a plot in the said Hotel/Motel Zone and the respondent No.2 duly approved the same for the amount of Tk. 34,50,715.00 (Taka thirty four lacs fifty thousand seven hundred fifteen). Thereafter, petitioner No.1 paid the first instalment of an amount of Tk. 8,64,926.00 (Taka eight lacs sixty four thousand nine hundre4d and twenty six) on 11.06.2005. The Government granted a long term lease for a period of 99 years to petitioner No.1 by lease agreement dated 04.07.2005. Lease agreement was duly registered and the petitioner No.1 paid rest of the installments of Tk. 8,66,274.00 (Taka eight lacs sixty six thousand two hundred seventy four) and Tk. 18,79,563.00 (Taka eighteen lacs seventy nine thousand five hundred and sixty three).

6. The government on 29.01.2006 formally handed over the possession of the said plot to petitioner No. 1 and Separate Khatian being Khatian No. 4365 was opened in the name of petitioner No.1. The petitioner paid the land rent regularly.

<u>7. The petitioner No.1 as per clause 6 of the lease agreement submitted the project plan and profile. The petitioner No.1 obtained clearance from the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism vide letter dated 16.10.2004. At the time of transfer to the petitioner No.1, there was no electricity, gas, water or even road connection to the said plot and as such, after obtaining clearance from the relevant authorities, petitioner No.1 could not start construction of the said project.</u>

8. On 06.04.2009 petitioner No.1 executed a Deed of Agreement with the petitioner No.2 company to construct Multi-stored hotel apartment building on the said plot and appointed petitioner No.2 as Constituted Attorney to construct the Hotel by registered general power of Attorney being Deed No. 1386 dated 06.04.2009.

9. After compliance with all the terms and conditions the petitioner No.2 started the construction work of the project on the said plot. Within six month time of the said approval, the petitioner has already constructed boundary and completed the foundation work as per plan, The petitioner No.2 has already invested an amount of Tk. 4,88,38,886.00( Taka four crore eighty eight lac thirty eight hundred eighty six) for the pilling works, foundation works, basement and column, labour cost and other expenses.

10. While the construction works were continuing in full scale, all on a sudden on 12.01.2010 the respondent No. 3, Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar, without serving any show cause notice, issued an official order on 12.1.2010 cancelling the permanent lease of the said plot and directed petitioner No.1 to handover the possession of the said plot to the government.

11. The petitioner being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned order of cancellation of lease has filed this writ petition and obtained the Rule.

12. The respondent No.1 Government has filed Affidavit-in-opposition and denied the statements and material allegations made in the writ petition and stated that in order to protect environment and ecosystem of the largest Sea Beach Area of Cox's Bazar, the Government was pleased to issue a Gazette Notification on 19.04.1999 and declared the area as the Ecologically Critical Area. According to the Gazette Notification the change of the nature of the land and water are prohibited due to declaration of Ecological Critical Area. The construction of Hotel/Motel in the ecological critical area in Cox's Bazar is totally illegal, because, it will frustrate the purpose of the said Gazette Notification.

13. It has been stated further that it is a Lease Agreement containing conditions which the lessee knowingly accepted. One of the conditions being that construction has to be made within 1(one) year from the date of lease agreement and for non compliance of that condition, the lesser can cancel the lease deed unilaterally and so, the petitioner representing the lessee at the very inception of the lease waived his right to challenge any action of the respondents, if taken pursuant to the said condition and hence, this writ petition is not maintainable. Moreover, by the irrevocable power of attorney the lessee has virtually for all practical purposes transferred the lease property to the petitioner which is violative of lease condition and since no prior permission of the government was taken before doing the saline as no such provision was there in the contract itself.

14. It has been stated further that the action of the respondents is based on objective material. The inter ministerial committee has inspected the site and found that there was no construction on the case plots. Even the petitioner in his petition also did not state that he had constructed within the period mentioned in the lease agreement. Hence, the allegation of arbitrariness or mala fide has no basis but the same allegation was brought against the government for fulfilling their misdeed and unplanned material gain.

15. It has been submitted that this Hon'ble Court in many cases have taken Suo Motto action by issuing Rule for the protection of climate and environment of Dhaka City, Rivers of Bangladesh and Saint Martin Island. It is in the fitness of things and the demand of the day that this Hon'ble Court would consider the necessity of preserving the natural condition of the sea shore which is the largest sea shore of the world and the same naturalness should not be affected by the construction of series of Hotel/Motel in the name of Tourism. Even, if the Government by way of its action invade the natural climate condition this Hon'ble Court is expected to interfere with that to uphold the constitutional obligation to protect environment which is included in the fundamental rights of every citizen of Bangladesh. Moreover, the intergenerational right of safe climate and natural environment is an obligation to protect the right to life as is enunciated in the decision of Supreme Court of Philippine and relied upon by our Appellate Division. Hence, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

16. The respondent No.2 filed Affidavit-in-opposition and denied the statements and material allegations made in the writ petition and stated that a plot being No. 16 consisting of 1.00 acre Khas land was given permanent lease to the petitioner and a lease agreement was signed on 4.7.2005 with some terms and condition. As per clause 11 of the terms of the lease agreement 'the construction work of the hotel/motel has to be beginning within one year from taking possession of the property and have to be completed within three years'. Though possession of the plot was handed over to the petitioner on 29.01.2006 but the petitioner has failed to complete construction work within stipulated time. As per clause 11 of the terms and condition of the lease agreement nothing is allowed to be constructed in the plot except Hotel/Motel. It is also stated that the lessee has submitted a written undertaking in stamp of Taka 150/-that he will be bound to follow the conditions of lease agreement. In clause 18 of the lease agreement, it was provided that `if any condition of the lease agreement is violated by the lessee in that case lesser has been authorized to cancel the agreement by his own decision'. In clause 19 of the lease agreement, it was provided that' if any condition is violated by the lessee in that case the agreement shall be treated as cancelled and the property will come to the control of the Government.' The petitioner violated the above mentioned conditions of the lease agreement, so the allotment was cancelled. No provisions were made in the lease deed that the petitioner will complete the construction work after electric connection, road construction and gas connection. So the plea of failure to complete the construction work is not related with the cancellation of allotment. The petitioner upon misleading the court obtained Rule and stay from the Hon'ble High Court Division.

17. The petitioner violated the terms and condition of the lease deed by selling 30 flats but the petitioner obtained the allotment only for constructing hotel in the plot.

18. At first, a committee was formed to examine the present status of the construction. After spot visit a detail report was submitted and then the petitioner was given opportunity to explain his position. The petitioner could not show that he has not violated the terms and condition of the agreement, so the cancellation order was issued.

<u>19. The statement of the petitioner is contradictory, because in the paragraph No.13 he stated that construction is going on. But in another paragraph the petitioner stated that construction could not be done due to absence of gas, road and electricity supply.</u>

20. It has been stated that lease deed was cancelled due to specific violation of the terms and as per the provision of the lease deed. So, it cannot be said that cancellation was made without following the procedure. It is admitted by the petitioner that the construction work of hotel has not been completed, so cancellation of allotment is not illegal.

21. The cancellation was made accordance with law, so question violation of fundamental rights does arise. It has been stated further that petitioner got opportunity to explain in of not the his position, so no principle of natural justice has been violated. In the terms of the lease deed, time was allowed for 3 years to complete the construction work, but the petitioner failed to comply with the terms. Due to violation of terms and condition of the lease deed the respondent issued cancellation letter lawfully. A sub-committee was formed by the government and the committee visited the spot on 21.07.2009 and went to every plot of the hotel/motel zone at Cox's Bazar and after hearing the lessee, they prepared a report and submitted to the inter ministerial committee. The committee has served notice upon the lessee and asked them to appear with necessary documents. Accordingly, the lessees were present at the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar and placed their documents to the sub-committee as well as participated in the hearing. Thereafter, the committee submitted detail reports mentioning the name of the lessee who has violated the terms and conditions of the lease agreement. Therefore, the Rule is liable to discharged because lease was cancelled due to violation of mandatory provisions of the lease agreement by the petitioner.

<u>22. The petitioner obtained the right and title in the property by virtue of allotment and is entitled to continue till existing of allotment. After cancellation of the allotment the petitioner has no right to hold the plot.</u>

23. In order to execute the policy of the Government, a committee was formed and after visiting the plots, they have submitted report stating the name of the lessee who has violated the condition of the lease agreement. It was specifically mentioned in the report that the petitioner violated the terms and condition of the lease agreement. Thereafter, according to the provisions of the lease deed the allotment was cancelled. Before issuing of cancellation letter, the petitioner was heard by the committee but he could not satisfy the committee due to his failure to complete construction work as per terms and condition of the lease agreement.

<u>24. The letter of cancellation of lease of the plot of the petitioner was served purely based on the ground of violation of the terms of the agreement which was admitted by the petitioner. So, it cannot be said that the cancellation letter was issued arbitrarily or malafide, rather it was issued lawfully. Moreover, the petitioner knowing fully about the terms and conditions of lease had signed the lease deed with the government. When it was proved through a report that the petitioner violated the terms and condition's of the lease agreement, at that time steps were taken to cancel the allotment of the plots of the petitioner and it was done lawfully.</u>

<u>25. The dispute arose between the parties arising out of contract against which, proper remedy is in civil court. Hence, the petition under Article 102 is not maintainable. Moreover, before cancellation of lease agreement an inter ministerial meeting was held on 28.05.2009 presided over by the Secretary, Ministry of Land. In the meeting a committee was formed headed by the Secretary, Civil Aviation and Tourism. The committee visited the plots at Cox's Bazar and found violation of the conditions of the lease agreement and submitted report about the violation of lease agreement. Moreover, the parliamentary Standing Committee of Ministry of Civil Aviation formed a committee comprising of 3(three) parliament Members and they have recommended for canceling the allotment. Considering all reports of violation of the conditions of the lease agreement decision was taken to cancel lease agreement.</u>

<u>26. So, any relief against the termination of allotment the petitioner may seek before the appropriate civil court. The petitioner was not treated other than in accordance with law, nor was any action detrimental to his property taken except in accordance with law. Therefore, the question of violation of fundamental rights of the petitioner does not arise.</u>

27. The respondent No.3 has filed affidavit in opposition and denied the material allegations made in the writ petition and stated that due to violation of almost all conditions of the lease agreement by the lessee, the Government lawfully cancelled the lease of the case land. It has been further stated that the statements that the petitioner invested crores of taka for the development of the said plots are not correct. After the registration of lease deed dated 04.07.2005 the petitioner did not take steps for long 5(five) years and thus the lessee hopelessly failed to construct Hotel/Motel within I (One) year payment of salami was mandatory as per schedule that is on 11.06.2005, 25.05.2006, 25.05.2007 and 25.05.2008 but the lessee paid the salami on 11.06.2005, 10.06.2006 and 09.04.2009 defying the conditions stipulated in the agreement in as much as:

“লীজ গ্রহীতা বন্দোবস্তি জমির অবশিষ্ট সালামীর টাকার নির্ধারিত কিস্তি চুক্তি মতে উল্লেখিত নির্ধারিত সময়ে পরিশোধ করিবে। নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে সেলামীর অবশিষ্ট অর্থ পরিশোধ না করিলে বন্দোবস্ত বাতিল বলিয়া গণ্য  হইবে এবং জমাকৃত অর্থ বাজেয়াপ্ত হইবে।”

28.  As per condition of lease agreement the lessee is not entitled to hand over the possession of lease hold plot in any manner to any other person, but the lessee transferred the possession by a General Power of Attorney dated 06.04.2009 and upon perusal of the deed, it would be seen that the petitioner has tactfully transferred the plot and therefore, the petitioner has violated the condition of the Lease Agreement and the government lawfully cancelled the lease of the case plots. In this connection it has been stated that as per condition of lease deed dated 04.07.2005 1(one) year specified in the lease agreement for construction of the Hotel. But the petitioners did not make any construction within the period stipulated in the lease deed. The inspection team of the respondents duly detected the same during inspection. It has been further stated that the petitioner No.1 has not mentioned when he made the construction as claimed by him. It is stated that the statements made about sale of Apartment in REHAB fair, is a clear proof (Annexure-F and F-1 of the writ petition) of violation of the terms of lease deed and thereby, set at naught the lease deed which was mainly intended for Hotel/Motel. It is stated that due to violation of almost all conditions of the lease agreement by the lessee, the Government lawfully cancelled the lease of the case land. The petitioner knowingly accepted the conditions and one of the conditions being that construction has to be made within 1(one) year from the date of lease agreement and in view of non compliance of that condition, the lessor cancelled the lease deed. So, the petitioner representing the lessee at the very inception of the lease waived his right to challenge any action of the respondents, if taken pursuant to the said condition and hence this writ petition is not maintainable. The action of the respondents are based on objective material. The inter ministerial committee has inspected the site and found that there was no construction on the case plots and the petitioner in his petition also did not state that he had constructed the Hotel within the period mentioned in the lease agreement. Hence, the allegation of arbitrariness or malafide has no basis but the allegation was brought against the government for illegal gain. It has been stated that this Hon'ble Court in many cases have taken Suo Motto action by issuing Rule for the protection of climate and environment of Dhaka City, Rivers of Bangladesh and Saint Martin Island. It is in the fitness of things and the demand of the day that this Hon'ble Court would consider the necessity of preserving the natural condition of the sea shore which is the largest sea shore of the world and the same naturalness should not be affected by the construction of series of Hotel/Motel in the name of Tourism. Even, if the Government by way of its action invade the natural climate condition, this Hon'ble Court is expected to interfere with that to uphold the constitutional obligation to protect environment which is included in the fundamental rights of every citizen of Bangladesh. Moreover, the intergenerational right to safe climate and natural environment is an obligation to protect the right to life as is enunciated in the decision of Supreme Court of Philippine and relied upon by our Appellate Division.

29. The writ petitioner had filed Affidavit-in-reply and denied the statements and assertion made in the affidavit-in-opposition and stated that all the actions of the petitioner were in accordance with the terms of the lease agreement, and the petitioner obtained all the necessary approvals/ permissions etc before commencing construction on the plot. Despite availing the facility to start construction work, the respondents in gross violation of the principles of natural justice and the laws of the land issued the impugned Memo to the petitioner. The petitioner never informed of any committee nor was given any report, whatsoever, which the respondent No.3 mentioned in the said paragraph.

<u>30. The writ petition arose out of the long term lease agreement granted by the District Collector, Cox's Bazar on behalf of the President of Bangladesh in exercise of his sovereign capacity. As such, the instant Writ petition is maintainable. The highest Court of the country has decided this point. The instant Writ Petition arose out of the action of the respondents in unlawfully cancelling the agreement of the petitioner with mala fide intention. The respondents as Government officials are to act in accordance with law and only in accordance with law. However, the respondents failed to do so by issuing the impugned Memo unlawfully even without giving any opportunity of personal hearing to the petitioner. The petitioner was never made aware of reports of any committees, inter ministerial meeting etc. Respondent No.3 in issuing the impugned Memo, has in effect acted at the direction of superior authorities and even for this reason the impugned Memo is liable to be set aside.</u>

<u>31. The respondents are in pursuit of taking away the vested right of the petitioner on the said plot by cancelling the lease and giving it over to other vested quarters. In issuing the impugned Memo the petitioner has violated the fundamental rights of the petitioner as guaranteed under the Constitution namely, Article 27, 31 and 42 of the Constitution. The respondents have exercised their authority not only in violation of the principles of natural justice but also with mala fide intention at the behest of interests of vested quarter.</u>

32. In W.P. No. 1473 of 2010 it has been stated that in the year 2002 the respondent No. 3 invited applications for allotment of plot in the Hotel/Mote zone of Cox's Bazar for the purpose of the constructing 1-5 star Hotels and Motels in the said area. Accordingly, the petitioner Company applied for allotment of a plot in the said Hotel/Motel Zone, on 01.07.2003 the petitioner Company submitted layout plan to respondent No.3 vide letter No. জঃপ্র/কক্ছ/রাজস্ব/২৪-১৭/২০০৩ dated 04.10.2003 who approved the plan for construction of 2 (two) star hotel. Thereafter, the Petitioner Company obtained height clearance from the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism dated 09.11.2003 and respondent No.3 dated 07.10.2003 confirmed the said clearance to the Petitioner Company. All the detailed procedure being complied with by the petitioner company, respondent No. 2 duly approved the application for allotment for consideration of Tk. 30,68,93.25 (Taka thirty lac sixty eight thousand none hundred thirty five and twenty five paisa).

33. Thereafter, the petitioner Company paid the full instalment of an amount of Tk. 30,68,936/- by treasury chalan on 07.01.2004 after which the Government granted a long terms lease for a period of 99 years to the petitioner Company by lease deed No. 853 dated 03.05.2006 for the said plot with reference to long term case No. 7/2002-2003.

34. On 29.06.2006 finally handed over the possession of the said plot to petitioner Company and the petitioner Company mutated the said plots in its name and a separate khatian being No. 4630 was created and had paid the land rent regularly.

35. Immediately, after getting possession of the said plot petitioner Company started developing the land of the said plot with its own finance to start the construction work and invested an amount of Tk. 51,03,100.00/- when the petitioner Company got the lease, there were no electricity, gas and water supply to the said plot and even today said services have not yet been provided and the petitioner needs those facilities in order to commence construction of the 2 (two) star Hotel.

<u>36. <u>"23. The notion that the public has a right to expect certain lands and natural areas to retain their natural characteristic is finding its way into the law of the land. <u>"Another major ecological tenet is that the world is finite. The earth can support only so many people and only so much human activity before limits are reached . This lesson was driven home by the oil crisis of the 1970s as well as by the pesticide scare of the 1960s. The current deterioration of the ozone layer is another vivid example of the complex, unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects posed by our disregard of the environmental limits to economic growth. the absolute finiteness of the environment, when coupled with human dependency on environment, leads to the unquestionable result that human activities will at some point be constrained. Human activity finds in the natural world its external limits. In short, the environment imposes constraints on our freedom these constraints are not the product of value choices but of the scientific impetrative of the environment's limitations. Reliance on improving technology can delay temporarily, but not forever, the inevitable constraints. Professor Barbara Ward has written of this ecological imperative in particularly vivid language. We can forget moral imperatives. But today the morals of respect and care and modesty come to us in a form we cannot evade. We cannot cheat on DNA. We cannot get round photosynthesis. We cannot say I am not going to give a damn about phytoplankton. All these tiny mechanisms provide the preconditions of our planetary life. To say we do not care is to say in the most literal sense that "we choose death." There is a commonly recognized link between laws and social values, but to ecologists a balance between laws and values is not alone sufficient to ensure a stable relationship between humans and their environment. Laws and values must also contend with the constraints imposed by the outside environment. Unfortunately, current legal doctrine rarely accounts for such constraints, and thus environmental stability is threatened. Historically, we have changed the environment to fit our conceptions of property. We have fenced, plowed and paved. The environment has proven malleable and to a large extent still is. But there is a limit to this malleability, and certain types of ecologically important resources for example, wetlands and riparian forests can no longer be destroyed without enormous long term effects on environmental and therefore social stability. To ecologists, the need for preserving sensitive resources social stability. To ecologists, the need for preserving sensitive resources does not reflect value choices but rather is the necessary result of objective observations of the laws of nature. In sum, ecologists view the environmental sciences as providing us with certain laws of nature. These laws, just like our own laws, restrict our freedom of conduct and choice. Unlike our laws, the laws of nature cannot be changed by legislative fiat; they are imposed on us by the natural world. An understanding of the laws of nature must therefore inform all of our social institutions."</u>

<u>24. The ancient Roman Empire developed a legal theory known as the "Doctrine of the Public Trust." It was founded on the ideas that certain common properties such as rivers, seashore, forests and the air were held by Government in trusteeship for the free and unimpeded use of the general public. Our contemporary concern about " the environment" bear a very close conceptual relationship to this legal doctrine. Under the Roman law these resources were either owned by no one (resnullious) or by every one in common (res communions). Under the English common law, however, the Sovereign could own these resources but the ownership was limited in nature, the Crown could not grant these properties to private owners if the effect was to interfere with the public interests in navigation or fishing. Resources that were suitable for these uses were deemed to b e held in trust by the Crown for the benefit of the public. Joseph L. Sax, Professor of Law, University of Michigan — proponent of the Modern Public Trust Doctrine —in an erudite article "</u>

<u>Public Trust Doctrine in Natural Resource Law: Effective Judicial Intervention", Michigan Law Review, Vol. 68, Part 1 p. 473, has given the historical background of the Public Trust Doctrine as under:</u>

<u>"The source of modern public trust law is found in a concept that received much attention in roman and English law- the nature of property rights in rivers, the sea, and the seashore. That history has been given considerable attention in the legal literature, need not be repeated in detail here. But two points should be emphasized. First, certain interests, such as navigation and fishing, were sought to be preserved for the benefit of the public; accordingly, property used for those purposes was distinguished from general public property which the sovereign could routinely grant to private owners. Second, while it was understood that in certain common properties- such as the seashore, highways, and running water- `perpetual use was dedicated to the public', it has never been clear whether the public had an enforceable right to prevent</u>

<u>infringement of those interests. Although the State apparently did protect public uses, no evidence is available that public rights could be legally asserted against a recalcitrant government."</u>

<u>25. The Public Trust Doctrine primarily rests on the principle that certain resources like air sea, waters and the forests have such a great importance to the people as a whole that it would be wholly unjustified to made them a subject of private ownership. The said resources being a gift of nature, they should be made freely available to everyone irrespective of the status in life, The doctrine enjoins upon the Government to protect the resources for the enjoyment of the general public rather than to permit their use for private ownership or commercial purposes. According to professor Sax the public Trust Doctrine imposes the following restrictions on governmental authority.</u>

<u>"Three types of restrictions on governmental authority are often thought to be imposed by the public trust: first , the property subject to the trust must not only be used for a public purpose, but it must be held available for use by the general public; second , the property may not be sold, even for a fair cash equivalent; and third the property must be maintained for particular types of uses.</u>

<u>33. It is no doubt correct that the public trust doctrine under the English common law extended only to certain traditional uses such as navigation, commerce and fishing. But the American Courts in recent cases have expanded the concept of the public trust doctrine. The observations of the Supreme Court of California in Mono Lake case clearly show the judicial concern in protecting all ecologically important lands, for example fresh water, wetlands or riparian forests. The observations of the Court in Mono Lake case to the effect that the protection of ecological values is among the purposes of public trust, may give rise to an argument that the ecology and the environment protection is a relevant factor to determine which lands, waters or airs are protected by the public trust doctrine. The Courts in United States are finally beginning to adopt this reasoning and are expanding the public trust to encompass new types of lands and waters. In Philips Petroleum Co. v. Mississippi the United States Supreme Court upheld Mississippi's extension of public trust doctrine to lands underlying non-navigable tidal areas. The majority judgment adopted ecological concepts to determine which lands can be considered tide lands. Philips Petroleum case assumes importance because the Supreme Court expanded the public trust doctrine to identify the tide lands not on commercial considerations but on ecological concepts. We see no reason why the public trust doctrine should not be expanded to include all ecosystems operating in our natural resource.</u>

<u>34. Our legal system-based on English common law- includes the public trust doctrine as part of its jurisprudence. The State is the trustee of all natural resources which are by nature meant for public use and enjoyment. Public at large is the beneficiary of the sea-shore, running waters, airs, forests and ecologically fragile lands. The state as a trustee is under a legal duty to protect the natural resources. These resources meant for public use cannot be converted into private ownership.</u>

So far as the third question is concerned, the contention of the learned Counsel of the appellants was that the learned Judges were wrong in dismissing the application for pre-emption since they ignored the doctrine of his pendens."

"10. The first question mentioned above required no further consideration as the point involved therein was already settled by the aforesaid Full Bench decision."

"6. The main thrust of the submission of the learned Advocate-on-Record is that action in allowing extension by the Government of the period for payment of the installment by the writ petitioner was wrong. We are not oblivious of the legal maxim "Commondum Ex Injuria Sua Nemo Habera Debet" i.e. no person ought to have advantage from his own wrong. We are, therefore, of the view that even any wrong is committed no one can take advantage of his own wrong to the prejudice of other. In the instant case however we do not find that there was any wrong in allowing the prayer of the writ respondent extending the time of payment of salami in the facts and circumstances. We further find that the writ petitioner complying with the direction for making payment within six months from the date of service of the letter dated 23.03.1992 discharged the duties and as such she cannot be punished for the alleged wrong. if any, committed by the Government. We like to add in this connection that the actions of the State should generally be in favour of protecting the rights of the citizens and should not, in the state of affairs as in the instant case, be aimed at causing prejudice taking away such right. We are thus of the view that the High Court Division did not commit any error in making the rule absolute.

455. Mr. Huq further contends that the authority cited by the learned Attorney General is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case in as much as in the said case the family of Kamal Nath (a former Minister for Environment and Forests, India) had direct link and had built a club at the bank of River Beas by encroaching land including substantial forests land. On the basis of the said case the Indian Supreme Court has developed a legal theory known as the "Doctrine of Public Trust" but in the instant case the petitioners have not encroached the Government land rather they have admittedly got lease of the land from the Government.

456. Mr. Mahbubey Alam contradicting the submissions of Mr. Huq the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioners submits that contents of the subsequent notification dated 3.5.1999 has to be read in its entirety in as much as he submits “কক্চবাজার জেলার ককবাজার টেকনাফ সমুদ্র সৈকত ও সোনাদিয়া দ্বীপ এর সংষ্লিষ্ট রিজার্ভ ফরেষ্ট এলাকাসমূহ বর্ণিত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লেথিত বিধি নিষেধের আওতা বহিভূত করা হলো। উক্ত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লিথিত অন্যান্য এলাকাসমুহ জারীকৃত প্রজ্ঞাপনের বিধি-নিষেধ যথারীতি বহাল থাকবে। and thereby it is clear that Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has not been excluded from the Ecologically critical area and also urged, the court to read the notification entirely in as much as he submits from paragraph 2 of the notification, it would be evident that the intention of the notification has clearly been expressed and if the entire notification is taken into consideration, it would be further evident that Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has not been excluded rather the reserve forest attached with Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has been excluded but not the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach and as such, the Sea Beach of Cox's Bazar has remained within the scope of Ecological critical area and thus, the government having violated the law at the relevant time had allotted the land to the lessees. He adds further that no body including the government can violate the law and again referring to the decision submits that the Indian Supreme Court having found that the Ilimachal Government had violated the law, Supreme Court of India itself quashed the lease agreement. He again submits that when anything is done violating the law in personal capacity or by the Government and in such case violation cannot be approved and again submits that the Rangs Building having been found constructed violating the law, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court directed to demolish the same and under the direction of the Appellate Division of Supreme Court the said Rangs Buildings was demolished.

457. In order to appreciate issues before us, we have to look into the Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act, 1995 (Act No. 1 of 1995) and it is pertinent to mention the definition and the relevant section on the basis of which the Government declared the area Ecologically Critical Area. The definitions are quoted below for ready reference:

Definitions. –

"Conservation of environment" means improvement of the qualitative and quantitative characteristics of different components of environment as well as prevention of degradation of those components; [ Ref Clause (f).]

"Ecosystem" means the inter-dependent and balanced complex association of all components of the environment which can support and influence the conservation and growth of all living organisms; [ Ref: Clause (g).]

"Environment" means the inter-relationship existing between water, air, soil and physical property and their relationship with human beings, other animals , plants and micro-organisms; [ Ref: Clause (d).]

"Environment pollutant" means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance which causes harmful effect to the environment and also includes heat, sound and radiation; [ Ref: Clause (e).]

"Pollution" means the contamination or alteration of the physical, chemical or biological properties of air, water or soil, including change in their temperature, taste, odor, density, or any other characteristics, or such other activity which, by way of discharging any liquid, gaseous, solid, radioactive or other substances into air, water or soil or any component of the environment, destroys or causes injury or harm to public health or to domestic, commercial, industrial, agricultural, recreational or other useful activity, or which by such discharge destroys or causes injury or harm to air, water, soil, livestock, wild animal, bird, fish, plant or other forms of life; [ Ref: Clause (b).]

"5.Declaration of ecologically critical area.- ( I ) If the Government is satisfied that an area is in an environmentally critical situation or is threatened to be in such situation, the Government may , by notification in the official Gazette, declare such area as an ecologically

critical area.

(2) The Government shall, in the notification published under suhn-section (1 ) A vehicle emitting smoke or gas injurious to health or environment shall not be operated nor shall such vehicles be switched on except for the purpose of test-operation for stopping the emission of such smoke or gas."

458. We have examined the above notifications regarding the declaration of Ecologically Critical Area along with submissions of the learned Advocates for the petitioners and the learned Attorney General for respondent No.1 (Government).

<u>459. There is no dispute as to the declaration made by the lst notification dated 19.04.1999 . Mr. Rafiq-ul-Huq, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach had been excluded by the subsequent notification dated 03.05.1999 and the lease was granted free from all encumbrances and having taken into consideration such submission we have very meticulously examined the notification dated 03.05.1999 by which certain areas were excluded from the declaration and found that</u>

<u>“ককচবাজার জেলার ককচবাজার-টেকনাফ সমুদ্র সৈকত ও সোনাদিয়া দ্বীপ এর সংশ্লিষট বিজার্ভ ফরেষ্ট এলাকাসমীহ বণির্ত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লেথিত বিধি নিষেধর আওতা বহিরভূত করা হলো।” Thus this clearly means that রিজার্ভ ফরেষ্ট এলাকাসমূহ বর্লিত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লেথিত বিধি নিষেধের আওতা বহির্ভূত করা হলো।</u>

<u>This means "Reserved Forest Area" of the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has been excluded from the Ecologically Critical Area but not the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach from the declaration of Ecologically Critical Area. We have no hesitation to accept the interpretation advanced by the learned Attorney General and in such circumstances, we hold that the lease was granted to the petitioners violating the declaration made by notification dated 19.4.1999. Therefore, we find no merit in the Rules.</u>

460. However, we direct as under:-

A. The Director General of Environment, Bangladesh is directed to appoint a Director having its office at Cox's Bazar to protect the area which have been declared Ecologically Critical Area relating to Cox's Bazar Sea Beach by notification dated 19.4.1999 and is further directed to demarcate the Ecologically Critical Area putting pillar within 6 months from date of receipt of the order.

B. The Director General is further directed to display Sign Boards depicting the area which have been declared by the aforementioned notification dated 19.4.1999 Ecologically Critical Area of the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach for public information and is tUrther directed to take appropriate step to maintain basic environment of the said declared area.

C. The Deputy Commissioner Cox's Bazar is directed to appoint a Commission consisting of not less than two Civil Engineers to ascertain the land to have been alloted to the petitioners along with the Construction cost to have been allegedly made in the land which have been leased out to the petitioners after receipt of the order.

D. The petitioners are directed to cooperate with the Commission in the process without creating hindrance and obstacle.

E. The respondent No. 1 is directed to return the consideration money to the lessee if they approach, the Secretary, Ministry of Land.

F. The respondent No. 1 is further directed to consider the application from the present lessees, if any allotment is given in future for construction of the Motel and Hotel in Cox's Bazar.

461. With the above directions and observations made hereinabove, the Rules are discharged without any order as to costs.

462. The orders of stay granted in all the writ petitions are thus vacated.
